chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad narrated from Musa ibn Umar, from Ibn Faddal, from Ghiyath, from Ja'far, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon him) who said:
Regarding a young orphan boy who was brought [to the Imam], he said: 'Take for his maintenance from the people of his clan who are closest to him, just as he inherits from them.'
ai.seo_question: Who is responsible for paying the expenses of an orphan in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the mechanism of *nafaqah* (maintenance) for an orphan, linking it directly to the principle of proximity in inheritance. It establishes that the financial burden falls upon the closest paternal relatives, ensuring the orphan's standard of living is preserved as if they were consuming their own share of the estate. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the extended family's collective responsibility for the vulnerable.
